incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Québec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions, CQLR c. S-31.1), arts. 6–36 (incorporation and articles), arts. 113–133 (directors and officers); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Loi sur la publicité légale des entreprises, CQLR c. P-44.1); Petroleum Products Act, CQLR c. P-29.01 (sectoral license for wholesale petroleum products).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Direction générale du registraire des entreprises, principal public registry and corporate registrar for Quebec enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) electronically submitted to the REQ, culminating in the Certificate/Attestation of Constitution and the publically recorded enterprise registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; shares may be issued without par value for consideration determined by the board, with no escrow deposit or capital blocking requirement. An attestation of consideration must be executed by the directors upon each share issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the Board ratifies the articles of incorporation of the Corporation, as duly registered by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, and approves the subscription, allotment, and issue of the Corporation's founding common shares for the consideration recorded by the Board; (2) the registered office of the Corporation at the civic address set out in the articles is adopted, and the Registraire is instructed to be advised of any change; (3) [Representative Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer, and [Name] is appointed Vice-President, each until successors are appointed; (4) the proposed by-laws and banking resolution are approved, and the officers are authorized to execute all certificates, declarations, licenses, and filings required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online enterprise register name search and reservation service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name clearance search in the REQ register and the Canadian federal trademark databases; verify the name is not prohibited, protected, or confusing under QBCA arts. 11–16 and the Charter of the French Language; file the compulsory name reservation request with the REQ (valid for 90 days) and obtain the reservation attestation to be appended to the articles.
required_dossiers: REQ name search report or attestation of reservation
Declaration of language compliance (French name version required in Quebec)
Identification documents of the incorporator and founding shareholders
Declaration of compliance executed by the incorporator (application of QBCA articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or challenged, submit a revised name requisition with supporting trademark evidence; alternatively, file an opposition or defensive name application with the Directeur des entreprises within the statutory objection window to preserve priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and filing of articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online constitution filing service of the Registre des entreprises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and execute the standard articles of incorporation (Form JA) specifying share classes and rights, transfer restrictions, number and constraints on directors, and any pre-emptive rights; attach each director's executed consent; file online with payment of the constitution fee; the REQ issues the Certificate of Constitution upon validation.
required_dossiers: Articles of incorporation (Form JA) executed by all incorporators
Consent to act as director signed by each initial director
REQ name reservation attestation
Civic address and mailing address of the registered office in Quebec
Proof of filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a deficiency notice under the Act respecting legal publicity, cure the defect within the prescribed period (generally 45 days) by filing an amended declaration, providing missing director consents, or correcting the address; if the file is closed, submit a new application with revised documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial registration and issuance of Quebec enterprise number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — legal publicity department (Registre de la publicité légale).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of constitution, file the initial registration declaration (déclaration initiale) online, stating the legal form, head office, registered office, directors, officers, and the primary activity code NAICS 424720 / ISIC 4661 (petroleum product merchant wholesale); the Registrar assigns the unique Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and renders the entry public.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution / attestation
Initial declaration form (statutory declaration of legal publicity)
Complete list of directors and officers with residential/professional addresses
Activity code selection sheet (NAICS 424720 / ISIC 4661)
Evidence of the Quebec head office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or defective filings accrue penalties under the Act respecting legal publicity; submit an online correction application (demande de modification/correction) within 30 days or use the voluntary compliance disclosures procedure to rescind accrued fines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance organization and statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel and corporate secretary acting for the board of directors; records maintained at the registered office (no governmental approval required).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting of the board; adopt by-law No. 1 in conformity with the QBCA model by-law; approve the share transfer register; issue share certificates to founding shareholders; appoint the President, Secretary-Treasurer, and other officers; adopt banking resolutions and signing authorities; preserve the minute book, registers of directors and shareholders, and the security register at the registered office.
required_dossiers: By-law No. 1 text and adoption resolution
Minutes of the organizational board meeting
Share subscription and certificate issuance records
Statutory registers (directors, shareholders, transfers, security interests)
Banking authorization and specimen signature resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Internal corrective remedy: amend or restate by-laws by shareholder special resolution; issue replacement share certificates upon proof of loss; rectify registers under QBCA provisions governing correction of corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and employer registrations with federal and Quebec authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (enterprise registration, QST, payroll accounts); Canada Revenue Agency (CRA, Business Number and GST/HST); optionally Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for import/export programs.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST), corporate income tax remittance and source deductions through the Revenu Québec online business account; apply to the CRA for a federal Business Number and GST/HST account using Form RC1; if the wholesale activity includes customs clearance or bonded fuel warehousing, open a CBSA importer/exporter account and post the required customs security.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution and NEQ (Quebec enterprise number)
Revenu Québec online registration application (QST and source deductions)
CRA Form RC1 for Business Number and GST/HST
CBSA import/export account application and customs bond evidence
Board resolution confirming designated officers and tax contact persons
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration data is mismatched, file corrections through the Revenu Québec and CRA secure portals; for late or challenged registrations, submit a voluntary disclosure to waive penalties and interest under the Tax Administration Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Régie de l'énergie du Québec — Direction des licences de produits pétroliers, acting under the Petroleum Products Act, CQLR c. P-29.01.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence de produits pétroliers (petroleum products licence) for the wholesale business (grossiste en produits pétroliers), authorizing the sale and marketing of marine fuel oil and refined petroleum distillates.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Department of the Environment, acting under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III — registration (déclaration) under Section 48 of the Environment Quality Act for a petroleum product storage and distribution depot; a full EIA (étude d'impact) is triggered only for terminals exceeding the thresholds of Schedule 1 (notably aggregate storage above 5,000 m³ or marine loading infrastructure) or for operations located in sensitive zones requiring a s. 22 or s. 31.1 authorization.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Operations must comply with the Regulation respecting petroleum products (Règlement sur les produits pétroliers): double-wall tank integrity, leak detection, secondary containment and spill prevention; marine fuel sulphur content limited to 0.10% within ECA waters under the federal Sulphur in Diesel Fuel Regulations and CEPA; fugitive VOC emissions and hydrocarbon vapour controls per the Code de gestion des produits pétroliers and CEPA schedule limits; any direct process-water discharge to natural waterways is prohibited absent a s. 22 environmental authorization, and sewer discharges must satisfy municipal by-laws and provincial water-quality criteria.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire safety service (service de sécurité incendie) under the Fire Safety Act, CQLR c. L-2.1; structural load and resistance certificate signed by a professional engineer for warehouses and tank foundations per the Building Act and Québec Construction Code; workplace health and safety inspection and prevention program clearance from the CNESST under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, CQLR c. S-2.1; and, for marine bunkering operations, Transport Canada clearance and compliance with the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 together with the applicable bunkering safety guidelines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) for federal corporate income tax (T2) and GST/HST outside Quebec; Revenu Québec (Agence du revenu du Québec, RQ) administers both the 5% federal GST for Quebec-based registrants and the 9.5% Quebec Sales Tax (QST) under the Canada-Quebec integrated tax administration agreement, with filing through the clicSÉUR Affaires portal; statutory business registry: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ); federal online portal: CRA My Business Account (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Determine Canadian nexus: a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada is subject to Part I tax for income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment and must register extra-provincially with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), obtaining a Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ). 2) Obtain the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1 (domestic) / RC151 (GST/HST registration for non-resident businesses); the BN is the statutory TIN for income tax, GST/HST, payroll and customs purposes. 3) Register with Revenu Québec for QST through clicSÉUR Affaires or Form LM-101-V; the QST account uses the BN followed by the program identifier 'TQ' plus a four-digit account number, while the provincial corporate income tax account is established concurrently with RQ for CO-17 filings. 4) File the initial declaration of registration (immatriculation) with REQ within 60 days of commencing activity and maintain a registered office and service address in Quebec. 5) For export reporting, enroll in the CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) / Canadian Export Reporting System (CES) to transmit B13A export declarations; a marine fuel and distillates wholesale brokerage operation also requires a sectoral petroleum products licence and compliance with Quebec's anti-money-laundering registration obligations for money services businesses if handling funds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Canada/Quebec business corporation (Inc./Corp.) is a per se taxable corporation under the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Business Corporations Act; resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income (ITA subsection 2(1), section 250(4)); no pass-through or fiscal transparency election is available; no tax-exempt zone applies in Quebec; a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada is taxed on Canadian-source business income attributable to a permanent establishment under Part I and may be subject to Part XIV branch tax on after-tax earnings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box regime; a Canadian business corporation cannot elect partnership or disregarded status. Available elections relevant to this energy-commodity trading dossier: (i) GST/HST section 150 election between closely related Canadian-resident corporations to treat otherwise taxable supplies as made for nil consideration; (ii) ETA section 156 election for nil-consideration supplies; (iii) ITA subsection 216 election permitting a non-resident to file a net-basis Canadian return for rental income; (iv) ITA section 219 election procedure for computing Part XIV branch tax on remitted branch profits; (v) hybrid mismatch rules (ITA sections 18.4-18.6 and Quebec equivalent) are self-executing effective 1 July 2022 for structured arrangements and 1 January 2023 for cross-border hybrid mismatch arrangements, with no elective entity classification; cross-border mismatches involving a transparent foreign entity or hybrid instrument trigger deduction deferral, deemed dividend treatment or primary/secondary adjustment consequences.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual value-added tax: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.5% computed on the GST-inclusive price, producing a combined effective rate of 14.975%; Quebec operates a pseudo-harmonized VAT administered jointly by Revenu Québec for GST and QST on supplies made in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 small supplier threshold measured on total worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) over four consecutive calendar quarters; registration for both GST and QST becomes mandatory once the threshold is exceeded; voluntary registration is permitted and commercially advisable for exporters to recover input tax credits (ITCs); the same C$30,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers with no permanent establishment in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Quebec mandates B2B electronic invoicing in phases: fiscal years beginning after 31 December 2023 for enterprises with annual turnover of at least C$500 million; after 31 December 2024 for turnover of at least C$50 million; and after 31 December 2025 for all enterprises. Invoices must be issued electronically in a structured format (XML/EDI or PDF with an advanced electronic signature) that guarantees authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility, and must be retained for six years. Canada operates no real-time fiscal clearance, API validation or digital stamping system; there is no continuous transaction control (CTC) government clearinghouse. Remittance of GST/QST returns is electronic through clicSÉUR Affaires (Revenu Québec) with EDI or direct-debit options, and Canada has adopted the PEPPOL network for Pan-Canadian B2G e-invoicing and public procurement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% GST/QST rate applies under Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Sales Tax mirror legislation to: (i) supplies of tangible personal property (crude oil, refined products and marine fuels) exported by the supplier or delivered to a common carrier for export, provided the goods actually leave Canada within 60 days of the time of supply unless the Minister extends the period, and documentary proof of exportation is obtained within two years of the supply; (ii) supplies of marine bunker fuel loaded as ships' stores on a vessel departing Canada on an international voyage, which are treated as exports at the time of bunkering; (iii) brokerage and commission services supplied to a non-resident in respect of exported petroleum goods where the service recipient is not a GST/QST registrant and the underlying goods are not situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; services relating to goods still physically in Canada (storage, blending, inspection, terminal handling) do not qualify for zero-rating and remain taxable at 14.975%. A registered exporter claims the zero rate and recovers input tax credits through the periodic GST/QST return; excess refunds are payable by Revenu Québec or CRA within approximately 30 days of filing, with statutory interest on late refunds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Export Declaration (Form A6) filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CES/CARM) or customs self-assessment portal
Ocean or inland Bill of Lading / sea waybill evidencing loading, foreign consignee and discharge port
Bunker Delivery Receipt (BDN) / vessel stores manifest and quantity survey certificate issued by the terminal or barge supplier
Customs-coded commercial invoice showing HS headings 2709/2710, INCOTERM, declared value and destination country
Sales contract, confirmation or charter party / voyage order
SWIFT MT103 or bank credit advice / inward remittance certificate evidencing settlement in freely convertible currency
Port clearance and vessel departure record (cargo/export manifest, port authority certificate of sailing)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canadian law imposes no express statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day parameter is adopted as the risk-rated settlement window for this dossier and aligns with the documentary cycle expected by CRA and Revenu Québec in export verification examinations. Mandatory compliance windows are: 60-day physical exportation rule (ETA Schedule VI), 2-year documentary-evidence window, and 6-year record retention requirement. If zero-rating is not substantiated, CRA or Revenu Québec reassesses the supply at 14.975% and claws back refunds with arrears interest from the filing due date; the normal reassessment window is four years, with no limitation period where misrepresentation, fraud or wilful default is established. Civil penalties include ETA false-statement and gross-negligence penalties of up to 50% of the tax avoided, ITA section 163(2) gross-negligence penalties of 50% of the understated tax, and Quebec equivalents under the Tax Administration Act. Criminal exposure arises under ETA sections 327/328 and ITA section 239 for tax evasion, with fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment of up to two years on summary conviction or five years on indictment; Customs Act export reporting offences carry fines of up to C$25,000 per occurrence, and CBSA Administrative Monetary Penalty System (AMPS) penalties apply to false or incomplete B13A declarations. Fraudulent export zero-rating also triggers mandatory disclosure reporting, revocation of registration, denial of input tax credits, and retrospective clawback of refunds with compound interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange and payment-system oversight is co-distributed to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential regulation, Payments Canada for clearing and settlement infrastructure (Lynx RTGS), FINTRAC for AML/CFT surveillance, and the Department of Finance Canada for sanctions and foreign investment policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Canada maintains no exchange controls; conversion, holding, borrowing, lending, and repatriation of currency are unrestricted. Profit and dividend remittances are governed exclusively by tax law: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax at 25% statutory, treaty-reduced under USMCA and CETA, with no FX approval required. A Quebec business corporation may maintain its books in USD for tax purposes under section 261 of the Income Tax Act (Canada). Non-resident equity investment is screened only through the Investment Canada Act net-benefit notification or review procedure, never through currency convertibility rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no holding-period constraint on foreign currency receipts. Marine fuel and distillate export proceeds may remain indefinitely in USD or any freely convertible foreign currency in Canadian or offshore bank accounts. The only compliance frictions are FINTRAC-reportable electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more and the usual income-tax recognition of export revenue under the accrual method.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (CAD and USD) plus Operational Trade Settlement Account
Operational Commodity Trade Account with Standby LC and Trade Finance facilities
Operational USD/CAD Clearing Account with Commodity Trade Finance line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Non-Canadian EMI and digital-bank platforms (Wise Business, Revolut Business, MultiPass) are not deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act and cannot provide commercial SWIFT MT103 settlement, documentary credit advising, standby LC issuance, or Lynx clearing. They are not participants in the Canadian high-value payment system and hold client funds through banking-as-a-service correspondents, creating principal concentration risk for a High_Risk_Special_License energy merchant. Their permitted role is confined to pre-funded disbursement cards, travel and small-vendor payments, and incidental FX conversion. A Canadian-based digital money service provider would require FINTRAC MSB registration and, under the new retail-payments oversight regime, authorization by the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act; none of these vehicles can substitute for a Schedule I treasury relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory hybrid onboarding with physical attendance for the high-risk tier. Canadian Schedule I banks allow secure digital submission of incorporation documents, but for a wholesale marine fuel and distillate trading corporation classified as High_Risk_Special_License, a physical interview at a Montreal corporate banking centre is a hard policy requirement. At least two directors, or one director plus the corporate secretary, must appear before the relationship manager with original passports and provincial ID for visual verification. Notarized board resolutions, the certified corporate register, and wet-ink signature cards must then be couriered. Fully remote opening is not offered for this risk tier except by select mid-tier banks accepting a live video interview witnessed by a Quebec notary or lawyer, and those accounts are typically restricted to CAD-only treasury without trade finance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sector classification: physical wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil and distillates; bank risk-based assessment flags the sector as High_Risk_Special_License where statutory permits and supply-chain traceability must be proven.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory export permits issued under the Export and Import Permits Act (EIPA); Quebec fuel wholesaler and environmental compliance registrations; federal or provincial certificate of status; 24-month audited or pro-forma financial statements; detailed trading business plan with named counterparties; internal AML/CTF policy manual and appointed compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: FINTRAC requires positive identification of every individual owning or controlling 25% or more of the corporation; nominee shareholders, offshore trusts, or unresolved ownership chains cause automatic refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized register of directors and individuals with 25% or greater ownership; FATCA and CRS self-certifications for each ultimate beneficial owner; certified passport pages and tax identification numbers; statement of source of wealth and source of funds; professional character references from a recognized Canadian law firm or CPA firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse media: U.S. OFAC, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), and United Nations Act sanctions screening of the energy commodity sector, especially any vessel, terminal, or counterparty in a sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified sanctions-compliance program; independently refreshed Dow Jones or LexisNexis World-Check risk ratings for each UBO and trading counterparty; signed end-user and non-sanctioned-jurisdiction undertakings; SWIFT message surveillance evidence; external legal opinion from Canadian and U.S. sanctions counsel confirming no prohibited dealings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large offshore inbound capital injection or shareholder loan within the first 90 days of onboarding; bank suspects structuring, layering, or round-tripping of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed equity subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement; source-of-funds bank statements of the originating legal entity; notarized board minutes approving the treasury inflow; home-jurisdiction tax clearance; Investment Canada Act notification receipt where applicable; written undertaking to provide quarterly lender and compliance monitoring reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: USD clearing nexus and maritime trade scrutiny: correspondent banks query vessel flag, cargo origin, port calls, and possible OFAC exposure of the physical bunker transaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trade package: sale and purchase contract with INCOTERMS 2020 clauses, bill of lading, cargo manifest, ISO 8217:2024 certificate of quality, bunker delivery note, vessel SIRE or OCIMF vetting report, customs entry documents, flag and registry certificates proving no sanctioned port calls, and any applicable Letters of Indemnity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Routing protocol: inbound funds from a non-resident parent or strategic investor are wired by SWIFT MT103, or by CHIPS/Fedwire for USD from US counterparties, to the Quebec corporations designated CAD or USD operating account at a Schedule I bank. Canada has no notification-based external purpose-code table comparable to a capital-control regime; remittance instructions must still carry accurate SWIFT fields: Field 50 ordering customer, Field 59 beneficiary, Field 70 remittance information identifying equity subscription, shareholder loan, or advance against a specific trade contract, and Field 72 bank-to-bank instructions. For equity injections, board resolutions, a notarized shareholder subscription agreement, and source-of-wealth statements are standard conditions precedent. FINTRAC large electronic funds transfer reports are mandatory for all incoming or outgoing transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, and transfers exceeding CAD 100,000 are ordinarily scrutinized through the banks enhanced due diligence unit for consistency with the approved business plan. Where the non-resident investor acquires control of the Quebec entity, the Investment Canada Act notification must be filed before implementation if the enterprise value is below the annual WTO threshold, or an application for review if above that threshold (approximately USD 1.179 billion in 2024 terms).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking for supplier and broker disbursements in USD, CAD, or third currencies; (ii) SWIFT MT700 issues and MT707 amendments of commercial documentary letters of credit under UCP600 for marine fuel and distillate purchases, with documents comprising commercial invoice, bill of lading, Certificate of Quantity and Quality, shore-tank or barge delivery proof, and INCOTERMS 2020 delivery terms; (iii) SWIFT MT760 standby letters of credit under ISP98 issued as performance, bid, and payment guarantees to physical suppliers and terminal operators; (iv) domestic CAD high-value disbursements are cleared in real time over Lynx, the Payments Canada RTGS system with final settlement at the Bank of Canada; (v) USD legs clear through the Canadian banks US correspondent on Fedwire or CHIPS with OFAC and SEMA sanctions screening applied at every hop. Payment conditions reference the ISO 8217:2024 marine fuel specification, including the 2% or 0.10% sulphur content limits for ECA compliance, with prompt payment and demurrage clauses incorporated in the supply contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CAD deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts, typically 1 to 24 months tenor, executed under a master FX agreement with an OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank
USD/CAD cross-currency swaps and FX swaps documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Credit Support Annex
European-style USD/CAD currency options purchased from a regulated Canadian dealer
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to restricted or illiquid bunkering invoicing currencies in emerging markets, provided they are not on Canadian sanctions lists

Commodity price hedging instruments, such as ICE Brent and New York Harbor ULSD swaps or futures, executed through a regulated commodity dealer or FCM, subject to the end-user hedging exemption from central clearing under the Quebec Derivatives Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the enterprise registration in Quebec, every calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file after the registrar's notice can result in cancellation of the enterprise registration and administrative strike-off of a Quebec-chartered corporation; reinstatement requires court or registry proceedings and publication. Monetary administrative penalties apply for late or false declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Annual Return (federal corporations only, if extra-provincially registered in Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the federal incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A federal corporation that defaults for two consecutive years may be administratively dissolved by the Director under the Canada Business Corporations Act; dissolution can revest assets and impose reinstatement costs and director exposures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Quebec CO-17 Corporation Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; both returns are aligned to that deadline if the fiscal year-end is used for Quebec purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per fully deferred month (maximum 12 months) under the Income Tax Act, compounded daily interest, and comparable Quebec interest and penalties; sustained non-compliance may lead to tax-driven enforcement and director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No universal revenue or asset threshold applies to private Canadian corporations. Audit is compulsory if the corporation is a reporting issuer under Canadian or Quebec securities legislation, is otherwise required by a regulator, or if shareholders fail to unanimously resolve to dispense with the auditor under the CBCA or QBCA. For a wholesale energy trading entity, banking, letter of credit and AML counterparties almost always impose a certified audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook Part I: IFRS as adopted in Canada for publicly accountable enterprises; Part II: Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is permitted for private corporations unless the regulator, lender or licence requires IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Share transfers are recorded in the internal securities or members register; they are not filed as a standalone public filing in Quebec. The annual declaration to REQ or the CBCA annual return functions as the annual confirmation that the registered office, directors and statutory records are accurate. The Register of Individuals with Significant Control must be updated within 15 days of any change involving 25% or greater voting or control rights; authorities may request access during audits and compliance checks.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholders' and directors' meetings and resolutions
Register of Transfers of shares and securities
Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 800 per year for a Quebec registered office and corporate agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - USD 35,000 per year for a certified audit by a Quebec CPA firm for a wholesale energy trading corporation with letters of credit and financing covenants

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
